survivingClaim: F_q[T] model, exact integers, q = 7 and 13, N = 2, 3, d <= 3, long marks (lam > N, lam > d), 58 configurations plus one optional; no statement about zeta. (i) Identity E = D + (SD - D) + CRperp + CRcoh, B = SB + CRcoh. (ii) |SD/D - 1| = O(N q^(N - lam/2)) by Weil's bound for a non-principal cubic character (measured <= 2.4e-3 for lam >= 7), so the excess over the diagonal is the cross term over pairs of distinct marked primes (c/(e-1) within 5e-5 of 1 for lam >= 10); random signs on the marked primes have mean energy SD exactly. (iii) Target a at q = 7 (2,12,1): e = 20.639, Cross/D = 19.639, B/D = 19.426. (iv) Registered rule c_perp in [-1.05, 1.5] holds in 593 of 596 and fails for the second target (c_perp 4.45, n 5.31), one U seed and mu; n <= 1.5 in 583 of 596; the label "excess = coherent cross" is not awarded. (v) Post hoc, at d = 1 only (7 rows, lam = 10, 12), the remainder of a, b and one U seed is a squared signal in the vector's own character at the row variable (specific: rank 1 of 63 sign directions); the d = 2 cases for mu and `one` are forced by a 2-dimensional symmetry space and carry no evidence; `one` at d = 3 open. (vi) At short marks, interior N >= 4 configurations show targets within control ranges (6 values); window-edge and N = 3 rows do not. (vii) The Z[omega] estimate (predicted term 1.5e-4 to 3.2e-4 of the diagonal against resolution 0.01; visibility near 1e10 columns) is an argued float proxy. Target not separated from random multiplicative signs (50 of 51). R1-R4 all false.
